paragraphs: In early November, people from the travel industry gather in London for a large travel event called WTM London. On November 3, 2026, at the start of the event, a new report came out. It is called the WTM Global Travel Report. A company named Tourism Economics made it, and it covers more than 185 countries.

The report says 2026 will be a record year. It expects 1.57 billion international overnight arrivals around the globe. An overnight arrival is a visitor from another country who stays at least one night. That is 2% more than in 2025.

But growth is slowing. In 2025, arrivals grew only 2%, down from 6% the year before. Tourism Economics gives three reasons. They are the conflict in Iran, higher prices for jet fuel, and the high cost of living.

The Middle East was hit the hardest. Overnight arrivals there fell 40% in 2026. During the conflict, many flights between Europe and Asia could not go through the region. Many long trips rely on transit airports in the Gulf, where passengers change planes. In 2025, these airports handled 15% of all transit around the globe.

So travelers are adapting. Many now choose places that are closer to home and less distant. Europe is one of the winners. Arrivals there are expected to grow 5% this year. For now, trips to distant places are less popular.

Travelers are also more careful with money. In 2026, one in six travelers chose their last international destination because it was good value for money. In 2025, it was about one in 11. But they do not simply spend less. More than half, 56%, said they like to save on some parts of a trip and spend more on others.
What is the main motivation for a trip? For 37% of travelers, it is the need to relax. In 2025, this number was 31%. So more people now travel with one simple motivation: to rest and relax.

Many travelers also rely on artificial intelligence, or AI, to gather information. According to the report, 58% would use AI to search for trips and compare prices. About half, 53%, would ask it for a recommendation. But only 36% would trust AI to finish a booking. In other words, people take a recommendation from AI, but most still book the trip on their own.

The prospect for 2027 is brighter if the problems of this year ease. Then international arrivals could grow 8%. If the conflict in Iran ends, arrivals to the Middle East could rise 43%. By 2032, the report expects 2.2 billion international arrivals.

Dave Goodger of Tourism Economics said travelers are more active in 2026 than ever before. They are adapting how and where they travel, but travel is still a key part of their spending. That seems a realistic picture. The report highlights a remarkable point. Even in a hard year, people do not give up travel. They look for trips that are closer, cheaper or calmer.
